title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. E/S is an elliptic curve with residue characteristics ≠ 2. M = E[4] is locally isomorphic to (Z/4)^2. M0 = M/2M ≅ E[2]. J ≅ M0* is the degree-3 étale cover of nonzero 2-torsion points, and M0 ≅ F2^J / F2(diag). The previous page says that giving M amounts to giving M0 (equivalently J) together with a torsor P under V_J(M0) ≅ End(M0) (≅ M0 ⊕ F2^ω, where ω is the degree-2 'orientation' cover attached to J). This page constructs that torsor.

The functor V_J. For any commutative group sheaf A on S, set V_J(A) = Ker(A^J → A), where the map is the sum (trace) along J. Étale-locally V_J(A) ≅ A^2. V_J is exact in A and commutes with base change.

The case 2A = 0. Then V_J(A) ≅ Hom(M0, A). A map F2^J / diag → A is exactly a function f: J → A with Σf = 0. Hence V_J(M0) ≅ End(M0).

The torsor. Apply V_J to the extension (39), 0 → M0 → M → M0 → 0 (sub M0 = 2M, quotient M/2M). This gives the extension (43): 0 → V_J(M0) → V_J(M) → V_J(M0) → 0, i.e. End(M0) → V_J(M) → End(M0).
- The canonical section of V_J(M0) is the inclusion J ≅ M0* ↪ M0, i.e. id_{M0} in End(M0).
- Its inverse image in V_J(M) is the torsor P_M.
- Concretely, P_M is the sheaf of maps J → E[4] lifting the inclusion J ↪ E[2] with trace zero. Its sections are triples of points Q_i of order 4 with 2Q_i = P_i (the three nonzero 2-torsion points) and Q1+Q2+Q3 = 0.

Check of the torsor property. Locally there are 4^3 = 64 lifts. Their sum lies in E[2] and can be killed by adjusting by E[2]-translates, leaving 16 = |End(M0)| sections. So P_M is indeed an End(M0)-torsor.

Purpose. This is the first step of determining M_{1,1}(4), the moduli of elliptic curves with level-4 structure. A full level-4 structure (épinglage) becomes a trivialization of J plus a section of P_M. The next page introduces the 'relative' épinglage (a section of P_M alone) and connects it, via E → E/(±1), to the x-line and the branch divisor (Δ).
errors: (43) ends with '→ 1' for an abelian sequence; it should be '→ 0'. This is a trivial slip.
The page leaves implicit that P_M is nonempty locally, i.e. that trace-zero lifts exist. This is easy: adjust the lifts by 2-torsion points.
The orientation of (39) has to be read correctly for (43) to give the right torsor: sub = 2M ≅ M0, quotient = M/2M = M0. The page does not spell this out, though the intent is clear.

ideas.what: Functor V_J(A) = Ker(A^J → A) attached to a degree-3 étale cover J. It is exact and compatible with base change, and equals Hom(M0, A) for 2-torsion A.
ideas.modern_name: Weil-restriction / trace-zero part (Res_{J/S}A)^{N=0}; the reduced permutation representation

ideas.what: The level-4 structure torsor: inverse image of id_{M0} under V_J(E[4]) → V_J(E[2]). It is the sheaf of trace-zero lifts of the three nonzero 2-torsion points to order-4 points, a torsor under End(E[2]).
ideas.modern_name: Torsor of lifts of a level-2 structure to level 4; fibre of X(4) → X(2) (Galois group Γ(2)/Γ(4) ≅ (Z/2)^3... here End(M0) of order 16 for the 'relative' version)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein, Fricke) for X(4)/X(2); modern moduli: Deligne–Rapoport, Katz–Mazur

ideas.what: Decomposition End(M0) ≅ M0 ⊕ F2^ω as a GL2(F2) = S3-module (from the previous page), applied to the torsor.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean, intrinsic, characteristic-free description of the fibre of level-4 over level-2 structures as an explicit End(E[2])-torsor built with the functor V_J. It is elegant and in typical Grothendieck style, but mathematically standard and well covered by the moduli literature (Katz–Mazur, classical Jacobi/Legendre theory).
transcription_corrections: Top line: '(12)' is the circled page number. The crossed-out words before 'la torseur' are illegible; 'plus allant d'avec' is doubtful.
Above each V_J(M0) term in (43), Grothendieck writes 'End(M0)' with a ≅ sign, identifying the extreme terms with End(M0). There is no phrase 'agissant sur les termes extrêmes'.
The line after (43) should read approximately '— pour A schéma (ou faisceau) en groupes commut. A sur S, on a'. The insertion is '(ou faisceaux)', not 'en faisceaux)'.
'(faisceau des noyaux : A^2)' is more likely '(faisceau loc. isom. à A^2)'.
'commutant [?] à bien sur au chgt. de base' should read approximately 'commutant aussi au chgt. de base'.
'Donc à une section de Z-modules finis [?] nulle de V_J(M0)' is unclear; it likely says 'Donc à une section canonique / évidente de V_J(M0)'.
'l'addition d'inclusion' should be 'l'application d'inclusion J ⥲ M0* ↪ M0', where M0* denotes M0 minus the zero section.
'(43) ... → 1' is as written in the manuscript; mathematically it should be '→ 0'.
